gaps.info: Age of infant (e.g., <28 days vs. 1–3 months)
gaps.discriminates: Risk stratification for serious bacterial infection (SBI): infants <28 days have substantially higher risk and different management thresholds than older infants; age directly determines whether empiric antibiotics and hospitalization are mandatory regardless of other findings.

gaps.info: Vital signs beyond temperature (e.g., heart rate, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, capillary refill)
gaps.discriminates: Systemic instability (e.g., tachycardia, tachypnea, hypoxia, prolonged capillary refill) would support sepsis or cardiopulmonary etiology and increase urgency, whereas stable vitals further mitigate SBI likelihood.

gaps.info: Detailed physical examination findings (e.g., fontanelle status, neck stiffness, rash, tone, alertness, cry quality)
gaps.discriminates: Findings such as bulging fontanelle, nuchal rigidity, petechial rash, or hypotonia would strongly suggest meningitis, sepsis, or metabolic/neurologic disorder — each altering diagnostic priority and management.
